name: happy
description:
One page of the computers collection plus the per-computer applications call each row triggers. Each computer's application row becomes a Software record, and `requests_absent` pins the tier that must NOT exist: GET /api/customers/{cid}/applications/{app_id}. A dead get_app_details() used to wrap that endpoint with its call site commented out; it could not have run as written (one argument passed to five parameters, in a function holding no credentials), and enabling it would have cost one request per COMPUTER-APPLICATION PAIR, not per computer. It was removed, and this assertion is what keeps it removed -- the licensing data it would have fetched is available from the whole-catalog endpoint in a single request instead. Proves the SLM envelope is unwrapped correctly -- the collection is `Body`, each row's fields are nested one level further under its own `Body`, and paging is driven by `Meta`, whose PageSize entry is absent on the last page and is the only thing that ends the walk.

The device-type mapping is what this file mainly pins. Snow does not publish a form-factor enum; it records the chassis as flags on the computer, and only the true cases say anything. IsPortable makes a Laptop and IsServer makes a Server, but a row with both false must carry NO deviceType -- it could be a desktop, a thin client, or the virtual machine that IsVirtual row actually is, and Snow has not said which. The virtual row is here precisely because assuming 'not portable, not a server' means desktop would type it wrongly.

CAVEAT worth knowing when reading this: the SLM Web API is hypermedia and self-describing, and Flexera publishes no resource schema for it, so these field names cannot be checked against a vendor reference. They are the ones the integration already read before this scenario existed. The mapping is written so that this cannot do harm -- a flag Snow does not return reads as false and produces no device type, rather than a wrong one.

namespaced_ids is skipped: the asset id is the bare SLM computer Id with no customer scope, so two Snow customers imported into one runZero account would collide. Pre-existing, not introduced here.
